findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` passes `order_by="-datetime"`, so `get_item_key` receives a `datetime` from each `AuditLogEntry`. This implementation calls `math.floor(value)`/`math.ceil(value)`, which raises `TypeError` for datetimes when `build_cursor` constructs the response cursors. Consequently every authorized request using `optimized_pagination=true` that returns audit-log rows will fail with a 500. This paginator needs DateTimePaginator-compatible timestamp conversion (or should subclass/reuse `DateTimePaginator`) rather than numeric rounding.

findings.title: Advanced negative-offset path uses unsupported Django queryset slicing
findings.body: The new advanced path intentionally passes a negative `start_offset` into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, but Django `QuerySet` does not support negative indexing or slicing and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` A client can supply a cursor with a negative offset, so an authorized user opting into this paginator can turn such a request into a 500 rather than receiving a valid page or a pagination validation error. Clamp or explicitly reject negative offsets; negative offsets cannot implement reverse traversal through ORM slicing.
